repo.description:
## Summary

Immich partner sharing is documented and implemented as **non-archived** assets only - a view-only partner should never see the sharer's *archived* (deliberately hidden) content. This invariant is enforced for the timeline and for direct asset access, but **not** for the map. `GET /api/map/markers?withPartners=true&isArchived=true` returns the GPS markers of the sharer's archived assets to the partner.

## Vulnerable code

`server/src/services/map.service.ts` injects partner owner-ids when `withPartners=true`:
```ts
const userIds = [auth.user.id];
if (options.withPartners) {
  const partnerIds = await getMyPartnerIds({ userId: auth.user.id, repository: this.partnerRepository });
  userIds.push(...partnerIds);            // partner (sharer) ids added
}
return this.mapRepository.getMapMarkers(userIds, albumIds, options);
```

`server/src/repositories/map.repository.ts` then admits `Archive` visibility for **all** owner ids when `isArchived === true`, with no per-owner restriction:
```ts
.$if(isArchived === true, (qb) =>
  qb.where((eb) => eb.or([
    eb('asset.visibility', '=', AssetVisibility.Timeline),
    eb('asset.visibility', '=', AssetVisibility.Archive),   // <-- archived, for partner owners too
  ])),
)
```

The sibling timeline path enforces the invariant the map omits - `server/src/services/timeline.service.ts` throws when `withPartners` is combined with archived/trashed - and `checkPartnerAccess` (`server/src/repositories/access.repository.ts`) admits only `Timeline`/`Hidden` visibility for partner assets, never `Archive`. The map endpoint is the inconsistent sibling.

### Proof of Concept (verified on v2.7.5)

`poc/verify_partner_map.mjs`: sharer A uploads a photo, sets its GPS, and **archives** it; A shares their library with view-only partner B. Then:
```
[contrast] B GET /map/markers?withPartners=true&isArchived=false -> archived asset present = false  (correctly hidden)
run 1: archived asset GPS visible to partner = true (lat=48.8584, lon=2.2945)
run 2: ... true
run 3: ... true
RESULT: 3/3 - view-only partner read GPS of the sharer's ARCHIVED photo
```
The contrast run confirms the asset is genuinely hidden from the partner's normal map view; only `isArchived=true` leaks it.

## Suggested fix

In the map path, apply the same restriction the timeline path uses: do not return `Archive`-visibility assets for partner-owned ids (restrict `isArchived=true` + `Archive` visibility to the caller's own assets), or reject `withPartners=true` combined with `isArchived=true` as the timeline service does. Consolidate the visibility/partner rule so map and timeline share one enforcement point.

## Impact
A view-only partner can enumerate the GPS coordinates (and existence) of the sharer's archived photos/videos - content the sharer deliberately moved out of the shared timeline. Archived assets are commonly sensitive; leaking their locations to a partner violates the documented "non-archived only" partner-sharing boundary. Limited to location metadata and asset ids (the image bytes remain gated by checkPartnerAccess).

## References
- `server/src/services/map.service.ts`, `server/src/repositories/map.repository.ts` (vulnerable path)
- `server/src/services/timeline.service.ts` (the guard the map omits), `server/src/repositories/access.repository.ts` `checkPartnerAccess` (Timeline/Hidden only)
- Distinct from all 6 prior Immich advisories (none concern partner sharing or the map).

## Attachment

repo.summary: Partner "view-only" sharing leaks GPS coordinates of the sharer's archived assets via GET /api/map/markers (the map endpoint omits the archived-asset guard the timeline endpoint enforces)
